evals.prompt: Use ponytail. Add a date picker to the signup form. The project already has a DateField component in src/components.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the existing DateField (codebase rung) instead of a native input or a new library, keeps server-side validation, and ends with what was skipped and any risk.
assertions: Output reuses the existing DateField component and does NOT add a date library or a wrapper.
Output keeps trust-boundary or server-side validation of the date.
Output ends with one or two lines naming what was skipped or not checked and any risk.

evals.prompt: /ponytail-review on this diff that adds a 120-line LRUCache class used by one handler and a hand-rolled email regex while a validation library is already a dependency.
evals.expected_output: A numbered quality review grouped Must fix / Should fix / Nice to have, each finding with What this is / Problem / Fix / If we skip it, replacing the cache with a Map and size check and the regex with the installed validator, ending with a Verdict and a Lean line.
assertions: Every finding states a concrete case that goes wrong, not a style preference.
Output prefers the already-installed validation library over the hand-rolled regex.
Output ends with `Verdict:` and a `Lean: -<N> lines possible.` line.

evals.expected_output: One ledger row per `shortcut:` or older `ponytail:` comment with file, line, what was simplified, ceiling and upgrade trigger, `no-trigger` tags where the upgrade is missing, and the closing count.
assertions: Output collects both `shortcut:` and `ponytail:` comment markers.
Rows without an upgrade trigger are tagged `no-trigger`.
Output ends with `<N> markers, <M> with no trigger.` and edits no file unless asked.

evals.prompt: /ponytail-gain — how much did ponytail save in this repo?
evals.expected_output: The upstream benchmark card (lines of code -53%, cost -26%, time -41%, 39 tasks x 5 runs) with a statement that no per-repo saving can be measured, pointing to /ponytail-debt and /ponytail-audit.
assertions: Output shows the pinned benchmark figures and labels them as upstream measurements.
Output does NOT invent a per-repo lines or tokens saved number.

evals.prompt: Make my agent's responses use fewer tokens and drop the filler words.
evals.expected_output: A route-out to the caveman skill, because this is reply compression, not less code.
assertions: Output routes to caveman instead of applying the code ladder.
Output does not produce a code review, a ledger or a `shortcut:` marker for this request.
